definition: The derivative of the derivative, written $f''(x)$ or $\frac{\mathrm{d}^{2}y}{\mathrm{d}x^{2}}$; it measures how fast the gradient is changing.
A way to classify a stationary point at $x = a$: if $f''(a) > 0$ it is a local minimum, if $f''(a) < 0$ it is a local maximum, and if $f''(a) = 0$ the test decides nothing.

A point on a graph where the concavity changes, from concave-up to concave-down or the other way; if $f''$ exists there it equals $0$, but $f''(x) = 0$ alone does not make a point of inflexion, and the gradient there need not be $0$.
Bending upwards on an interval, with the gradient increasing as $x$ increases; a graph is concave-up on any interval where $f''(x) > 0$ throughout.
Bending downwards on an interval, with the gradient decreasing as $x$ increases; a graph is concave-down on any interval where $f''(x) < 0$ throughout.
